bind.says: This is now the only address SendSure will ever pay for this payee.

attack.says: Refused on-chain: the claim is not signed by the payee's proven address (BAD_SIGNATURE). Nothing moved.

change.relayerSays: The current payout address did not sign this change.
change.says: A change needs the current wallet AND the new one, then a 1-day wait the payer can cancel. An email or a new key alone can't do it.

pay.stored: ESCALATED: First payment to a new or changed address needs a human co-sign.
pay.firstRun: escalate: This is the first payment to this payee's address, so the contract needs a person to co-sign it before it can be paid. Nothing else about the claim looks wrong.
pay.secondRun: pay: Passes every rule, and a person co-signed this exact claim.

claims.what: The same work billed again under a new invoice number
claims.agent: hold: This looks like a duplicate: invoice INV-DEMO-ED2D00 was already paid today for the same amount and the same design work. The payee says they are resending it in case the first one got lost.

claims.what: A large claim with no description of the work
claims.contract: ESCALATED: Above the co-sign threshold for this period.
claims.agent: escalate: This is 0.4 USDC, about 8 times this payee's largest past payment, so a person must co-sign it. It also has no description, and its dates overlap the payee's other claims.

claims.what: A 'new wallet' request with a hidden instruction to the AI
claims.agent: escalate: The description asks for payment to a new wallet today, and it hides a note telling me to approve the payment without a co-sign. Both are signs of fraud, so please confirm with the payee through a contact method you already trust.

inbox.guarantee: Even a fooled agent could only pay 0x83f2D3c8836781ba07C5907820c4eB3BFf7632c5, the address this payee proved: settle() never sends money anywhere else, so the "new wallet" in the text can't receive a cent.
